audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer carried a blanket 'Skill' on all seven rows while the content layer already read Ziggs / Skill / Skill / Skill / Lux / Lux / Skill — rows 0, 4 and 5 rendered two different answers.
audit.why: The content chart matches the kits: Ziggs edges level 1 on cooldown and mana (Bouncing Bomb 6s / 50 mana vs Lux E 10s / 70 mana), Lux takes 6 and first item because Final Spark plus a landed Light Binding is single-target kill pressure Mega Inferno Bomb does not answer, and it evens late when Satchel Charge and Hexplosive Minefield zone the fight.
audit.corrected: phases[0].side -> Ziggs, phases[4].side and phases[5].side -> Lux. win[N] already held those values, so no paired content edit was written (a no-op would take the chart group down).

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[0].why described Lux out-poking from max range, which contradicted the Ziggs row it now sits under.
audit.why: Lux E is 1100 and Q 1175 against Bouncing Bomb's 850, so range is not why he wins level 1 — frequency is. His Q is 6s for 50 mana against her 10s, 70-mana E.
audit.corrected: phases[0].why rewritten to the cooldown-and-cost reason. Lux's own spikes (6, first item) left where the content layer already put them.

audit.whatIsWrong: No Ziggs ability was ever named (packet defect), breakdown.cooldowns held no digit (lint), and the Short Fuse auto-reset tell was absent entirely.
audit.why: Satchel Charge 20/18/16/14/12s is his only escape and knocks him away, so a Light Binding only converts while it is down. Bouncing Bomb 6/5.5/5/4.5/4s is the chip engine. Hexplosive Minefield is a flat 16s. Short Fuse is an empowered-auto reset whose cooldown shortens every time he casts, so the wind-up is the step-back cue, not the spell.
audit.corrected: Cooldowns field rebuilt with real numbers; dosFull[1].d now carries the Short Fuse / Illumination auto tell; dontsFull[2].d contrasts Mega Inferno Bomb's 5000 range with Final Spark's 3340.

audit.whatIsWrong: The missing-interactions file flags that Satchel Charge carries a percent-health component, so flat MR is not the answer to it.
audit.why: The kit's percentHealth flag is a derived flag and Riot's own Satchel Charge text does not describe percent-health damage, so I did not write it into the page.

edits.before: E-poke from max range on his last-hits — the slow zone plus passive auto is your chip engine from level 1.
edits.after: His Bouncing Bomb is a 6s cooldown for 50 mana against your 10s E — he simply gets more level-1 poke than you do.

edits.before: - Ziggs Satchel Charge: matchup-defining — His knockback escape — he is catchable only while it is down. It governs your forward steps. - W Prismatic Barrier spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Satchel Charge is 20s at rank 1 and 12s at rank 5 — his only escape, so the root only converts while it is down. - Bouncing Bomb is 6s at rank 1, 4s maxed: constant chip. - Hexplosive Minefield is a flat 16s zone, so a dodged minefield is 16 seconds of free walking.

edits.before: E the contact, detonate, weave the passive auto, and keep Q visibly loaded — the chip is free and the root threat does the zoning.
edits.after: Illumination detonates on your next auto, and Short Fuse does the same for him — his wind-up is the tell to step back, not his cast.

edits.before: Q-poking on cooldown and facing the dive with an empty root slot — Lux without the binding banked is everyone's favorite snack.
edits.after: Mega Inferno Bomb clears from 5000 range and yours does not — spend Final Spark on the pick you can see, not on the wave he can push.

edits.before: Ziggs wins by landing Satchel Charge, denying your pattern, and out-ranging your plan one polite trade at a time.
edits.after: Ziggs wins by chipping you with a 4-second Bouncing Bomb, mining the ground you need, and Satchel-jumping out of the root.

edits.before: Carry through the root-laser pipeline — one binding per fight, converted at screen range; your job is owning the geometry that makes it land.
edits.after: Carry by punishing the Satchel: it is 20s early, and every root that lands inside that window converts to a kill his kit cannot answer.

edits.before: Ahead, own the geometry: E Ziggs off every contact, root the answers, and laser the river fights from fog — fed Lux turns vision lines into kill lines.
edits.after: Ahead, hunt the Satchel window: bait it with a step-up, root him the moment it is spent, and take the wave and the plates he can no longer defend.
